ui_answer: Under SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 2026, mutual funds may borrow up to 20% of the net assets of a scheme to meet temporary liquidity needs such as unit repurchase, redemption, interest payment or Income Distribution Cum Capital Withdrawal payouts, and the borrowing period must not exceed six months [1]. For intraday borrowings, the 20% cap does not apply; instead, the amount is limited to the guaranteed receivables due on the same day from the Government of India, RBI, and Clearing Corporation of India Limited [1].
